sections.future_developments: Future developments The group will continue to consist of a parent holding company, with shares held in trading subsidiaries as detailed in note 15. The operational management of 2 football clubs will continue, and the management team will continually seek new opportunities to offer additional football related services and experiences. The digital agency activities undertaken by The Leisure Channel Ltd ceased in 2025. The decision was made for the subsidiary to continue to exist for a period of time while assets are realised, debts collected and external liabilities paid. The Leisure Channel Ltd was dissolved on 17 February 2026. Auditor The auditor, Sumer Auditco Limited, is deemed to be reappointed under section 487(2) of the Companies Act 2006. Statement of director's responsibilities The director is responsible for preparing the Annual Report and the financial statements in accordance with applicable law and regulations. Company law requires the director to prepare financial statements for each financial year. Under that law the director has elected to prepare the financial statements in accordance with United Kingdom Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (United Kingdom Accounting Standards and applicable law). Under company law the director must not approve the financial statements unless he is satisfied that they give a true and fair view of the state of affairs of the group and company, and of the profit or loss of the group for that period. sections.principal_risks: Principal risks and uncertainties - Group The group seeks to manage risk through a combination of board oversight, operational routines, and policies. The principal risks are aggregated as follows: Liquidity risk The group seeks to manage financial risk by ensuring liquidity is available to meet foreseeable needs and to invest cash assets safely and profitably. For short to medium term flexibility, from time to time related parties provide cash loans. Industry specific risks The principal risk to the club is poor on-field performance, resulting in relegation that would undoubtedly impact the club’s income levels. The club remains in the EFL Sky Bet League Two, with the director continues to monitor the effectiveness of the business model to mitigate such risk of relegation. The group is impacted directly by the regulations and rules set by the FAI, FA, EFL, UEFA, and FIFA. The board monitors any changes within these regulations and ensure compliance to them. Key performance indicators - Group The Director has, and will continue to, monitor all of the Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and daily operating controls and maintain a strong focus on increasing performance of the group. sections.strategic_report: Strategic report 1 - 3 Director's report 4 - 6 Independent auditor's report 7 - 9 Group statement of comprehensive income 10 - 11 Group balance sheet 12 Company balance sheet 13 Group statement of changes in equity 14 Company statement of changes in equity 15 Group statement of cash flows 16 Notes to the financial statements 17 - 36 THE WILLOWS 96 HOLDINGS LTD STRATEGIC REPORT FOR THE YEAR ENDED 30 JUNE 2025 \- 1 - The director presents the strategic report for the year ended 30 June 2025. Review of the business - Group The company was incorporated on 14 June 2023. During the previous period the company acquired shares at deemed fair value in Fleetwood Wanderers Limited, The Leisure Channel Ltd and Power Grade Limited. The company from herein is an investment holding company. Details of the subsidiaries are provided in note 15. Review of the business - Fleetwood Wanderers Limited The club commenced the 2024/25 season with Charlie Adam as Head Coach, starting their first season in the EFL Sky Bet League Two since 2014. The club ended the season with Peter Wild as Head Coach. The club continues to invest strongly in the academy, maintaining category 2 status being one of only three clubs to hold this status whilst playing in the EFL Sky Bet League Two. In line with the club’s business model of investing into the academy through personnel and infrastructure, the club continues to realise income from the sale of academy players and negotiated transfer clauses on those players, allowing for significant future sell on percentages and other ongoing payments, contingent on the performances of those players at their new clubs. The expectation is that this income stream will continue to the benefit of the club year on year, both from the future movement of players sold and with more academy players playing for the 1st team, through this continued investment and development of new young talent at the club. Several academy players made their 1st team debuts, illustrating the ongoing success of the commitment to invest in the development of the club and its players. The club continued to work with Waterford FC, Ireland, in a collaboration to extend the recruitment and development options for the club. The link saw a number of players transfer between the clubs during the season. The club continues to utilise the Poolfoot Farm Training Facility, ensuring that state-of-the-art facilities are available throughout the whole club structure from the 1st team to all age groups throughout the academy. Review of the business - Power Grade Limited Waterford Football Club is an Irish association football club based in Waterford, Ireland, competing in the League of Ireland Premier Division. Following promotion to the Premier Division, the club finished 7th in the 2024 season and subsequently retained its status for the 2026 season, finishing 9th in the 2025 league campaign and securing survival via the relegation play-off. The club continues to operate in conjunction with its sister club, Fleetwood Town, with arrangements in place for the sharing of expertise and the movement of players between the two clubs. This structure supports player development and squad management. During the 2025 financial period, the club established a Women’s Team, which competed in the League of Ireland Women’s Premier Division for the first time. In addition, the club implemented a number of operational developments, including obtaining the appropriate licensing to permit alcohol sales on match days, expanding food and beverage provision, and introducing an updated ticketing system and website platform. These activities represent continued operational development of the club across both sporting and commercial functions during the period.
